name: Sherlock
notes: Free open-source CLI, no signup and no hosted API, so there are no API credentials to obtain. Only third-party MCP servers exist. The agent read 'free' as free self-serve access and derived 'ready to build'; free describes the tool, not credentials that do not exist. Enum mapping agreed with Claude, observations mine.

name: Mermaid CLI
notes: Free open-source CLI with a Node.js API, no signup and no hosted endpoint, so there are no API credentials to obtain. Only third-party MCP servers exist, nothing official from the Mermaid project. The pipeline left access null rather than misreading it, which is the right call here. Enum mapping agreed with Claude, observations mine

name: iPayX
notes: The page at /developers/sandbox is titled 'Sandbox Reference' but only documents generating a live key (ipx_live_...) directly from /developers, with plan-based usage limits (Starter/Pro/Enterprise), no separate sandbox-key type and no review step to reach production. Odd naming worth flagging on its own.

name: Commas (formerly fanbasis)
notes: Rebranded from fanbasis to Commas. SDK offering is a hosted checkout embed and React SDK (@fanbasis/checkout-react), not a general-purpose API client SDK, worth noting since it could be misread as SDK-only access. api_breadth of medium comes from the 44 built-in tools cited on the MCP and CLI docs pages.

name: Waterfall.io
notes: No public rate card or self-serve signup; pricing page ends with 'Book a call to hear more,' quoted only after a benchmark on the customer's own data. No MCP mentioned anywhere on the docs intro page checked.

name: NotebookLM
notes: The free consumer NotebookLM has no public API at all. Only Gemini Notebook Enterprise (the renamed NotebookLM Enterprise, a paid Google Cloud product) has a documented API. Getting access needs a GCP project, enabling the Discovery Engine API, and org identity provider setup (Cloud Identity or Workforce Identity Federation), which is real admin-level configuration, not a quick solo-developer signup, even though a 14-day free-trial subscription tier exists alongside the paid tiers. Filed as free trial since that tier exists without paying or contacting a Google salesperson, but the admin/IdP setup burden is closer to admin approval in practice.

name: Consensus
notes: Docs at docs.consensus.app describe the API as self-serve with a free plan, but the actual access page requires contacting customer support for individuals and filling out a form for organisations. Docs and real access flow disagree here, worth flagging as a case where documentation overstated self-serve access.

name: PitchBook
notes: The API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform requiring a standalone contract agreement; access always routes through their Direct Data team regardless of whether you're an existing customer. The 'Request free trial' CTA on the page is for the general platform, not a self-serve path to API credentials. Auth described only as 'an API key or authentication token,' exact scheme not specified.

name: DealCloud
notes: You need an existing DealCloud site and your org's admin must enable the 'API' capability for your user group before you can generate a key. Auth is a real OAuth2 Client Credentials flow (client_id + apiKey exchanged for a scoped bearer token expiring every 15 minutes), not a plain static API key. api_breadth is an estimate from 7 named functional areas (Authentication, User Management, Schema, Data, Backups, Publications, Relationship Intelligence), each with multiple endpoints, no exact endpoint count given.

name: Salesforce
notes: Official Salesforce Hosted MCP servers are GA only for Enterprise Edition orgs and above, not the free Developer Edition used for API access itself, worth keeping those two facts separate. api_breadth of large is based on general knowledge of the REST/SOAP/Bulk/Metadata API family, not a specific counted quote from a fetched page.

name: Plain
notes: Base GraphQL API uses API keys tied to Machine Users; the separate official MCP server uses OAuth2 tied to your own Plain account instead, worth keeping those two auth paths distinct. api_breadth is unknown because it's a single GraphQL endpoint, not a countable REST endpoint list; the MCP layer separately documents 30 tools, which is a different measure. Pricing has no permanent free tier, only a 7-day free trial across paid plans.

name: Zoho Cliq
notes: Zoho Cliq has a free plan for unlimited users and free self-serve signup; the OAuth2 client registration goes through the standard Zoho API Console. api_breadth is unknown, no endpoint count is given on the intro page. No MCP mentioned anywhere in the docs checked.

name: Meta Ads
notes: Development access (roles on the app itself) is self-serve and free. Anyone using the app without a role on it requires App Review plus Business Verification before the app can go Live, which is the prod_requires_review case this schema is built to capture. No official MCP found. api_breadth is large based on the well-known size of the Marketing API family, not a specific counted quote.

name: Squarespace
notes: Generating a Developer API key for a custom application specifically requires the Commerce Advanced plan, a particular paid tier, not just any active site. OAuth-based Extensions are available on any plan but go through a separate 'become a registered OAuth client' process. api_breadth of medium is estimated from the 7-8 named Commerce API categories (Forms, Inventory, Orders, Products, Contacts, Discounts, Webhook Subscriptions, Transactions), not a counted total.

name: MrScraper
notes: Free plan (100 tokens/month) requires no credit card, so access is genuinely self-serve. Official MCP server source is on GitHub for local setup, but it's MrScraper's own product, so counted as official rather than community. api_breadth is unknown, no endpoint count given.

name: Sentry
notes: Sentry supports both auth tokens (Bearer, self-serve, no consent screen) and OAuth2 (for third-party apps acting on behalf of users). Filed as Bearer since that's the primary self-serve path for using the API yourself. Free Developer plan exists forever, no credit card, and MCP is included even on that free plan. api_breadth of large is based on the 20+ endpoint categories listed in the sidebar (Organizations, Projects, Events, Dashboards, Monitors, Releases, Teams, Users, Profiling, Replays, SCIM, etc), not a counted total.

name: Coda (rebranded to Superhuman Docs)
notes: Coda has been rebranded to Superhuman Docs; the docs URL (coda.io/developers/apis/v1) now redirects to docs.superhuman.com. Same API, same base endpoint (coda.io/apis/v1), just renamed. Docs explicitly say the API is 'available to all of our users free of charge, in both free and paid workspaces,' though some operations need Doc Maker status. api_breadth is unknown, no endpoint count captured from what was fetched.

name: Brex
notes: Generating a user token requires signing in as an account admin or card admin on an actual Brex account, and the company must accept Brex's developer API agreement first, so this isn't a solo-developer signup, you need to already be a Brex business customer with admin rights. Only a production API server exists, no sandbox mentioned. api_breadth of medium is estimated from the 10 named functional API areas (Accounting, Budgets, Expenses, Fields, Onboarding, Payments, Team, Transactions, Travel, Webhooks), not a counted total. No MCP mentioned.

name: higgsfield
notes: Auth is a nonstandard 'Authorization: Key {key_id}:{key_secret}' scheme, not Bearer, Basic, or OAuth2, so filed as custom. Credentials are created and managed in the Higgsfield Console (self-serve signup implied), but no free-tier or pricing page confirmed the actual access tier during this check, so access is left null rather than guessed. Docs mention using separate credentials for development and production as a hygiene practice, not a documented review process, so prod_requires_review stays null too. api_breadth is unknown, no endpoint count found.
